sections.h2: How did Warner Robins grow from a farm stop into Georgia's 11th largest city?
sections.html:
Warner Robins began as the farming community of Wellston, which took its present name on September 1, 1942, after the War Department chose Houston County for an air depot. The town was incorporated in March 1943 and became a city in 1956, per Wikipedia. The census found 50 people here in 1940, 7,986 in 1950 and 80,308 in 2020.

Robins Air Force Base lies just east of the city limits, across U.S. Highway 129, and it still anchors the local economy. The city sits roughly 20 miles south of Macon and 100 miles south of Atlanta, covers about 38 square miles, and straddles Houston and Peach counties. Its nickname is the International City.

Weather is part of the housing story. The city has a humid subtropical climate with hot summers, and an F4 tornado on April 30, 1953 killed 18 people and damaged part of the base. Tornado activity in the Warner Robins area has run above the state average.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about homes in Warner Robins?
sections.html:
Warner Robins is a renter-heavy city with homes priced well below the national level. QuickFacts shows an owner-occupied rate of 53.5% for 2020-2024, against 65.2% for the United States.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $185,700, compared with $332,700 nationally.
  • Median gross rent: $1,212.
  • Median household income: $66,970.
  • Households: 31,930; veterans: 8,651.
  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 87,761, up from 80,308 in 2020.

The 2020 census counted 34,191 housing units, of which 7.4% were vacant, and the median age was 34.1. With a median age that young and an owner rate near 54%, rental houses make up a large part of the stock. The figures come from the Census Bureau.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Warner Robins?
sections.html:
Houston County runs the assessment and collection offices, and the City of Warner Robins sets its own millage rate. The city spans two counties, Houston and Peach, so owners with a Peach County parcel should ask the Peach County Tax Commissioner how their bill is handled.

  • Houston County Tax Commissioner, Warner Robins office: 202 Carl Vinson Parkway, Warner Robins, GA 31088, (478) 542-2110, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Perry office: 201 Perry Parkway, (478) 218-4940.
  • Property tax questions by email: taxquestions@houstoncountyga.gov.
  • Houston County Tax Assessors, 201 Perry Parkway, Perry: (478) 218-4750 for real estate values; parcel data is on qPublic.
  • City of Warner Robins: (478) 929-1148 for billing questions, as listed on the county assessor's FAQ.

The assessors' office states that it does not handle billing, and the commissioner's site states that the commissioner does not set value or millage.

sections.h2: What is the City of Warner Robins millage rate?
sections.html:
The Mayor and Council adopted a 2026 rate of 10.000 mills on September 22, 2026. That is 1.047 mills above the 2025 rate of 8.953 mills, according to the city's announcement.

The city also pointed to the Floating Homestead Local Option Sales Tax approved by Houston County voters in May 2026, which is meant to reduce property taxes over time. The city expects 2028 to be the first full calendar year of that revenue. County and school millage are separate from the city's rate and appear on your own bill.

sections.h2: When are Warner Robins property taxes due?
sections.html:
Houston County mails real estate bills before October 20, and the tax is due December 20 of the same year. After the due date, interest is added monthly at the rate set by law, and a 5% penalty is added after each 120 days, up to a total of 20%.

Partial payments are accepted. Taxes unpaid for more than 90 days can be recorded as a lien with the Clerk of Superior Court, and the Tax Commissioner can levy on the property as a last resort. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, with bills mailed in January and a decal issued on payment.

The county's site says bills go to the homeowner and never to the mortgage company, so forward the bill to your lender if it pays from escrow.

sections.h2: How do exemptions and appeals work in Houston County?
sections.html:
File a homestead application with the Houston County Tax Assessor's Office by April 1 of the first year you want it. Applications received later start the following year, and the exemption renews automatically until your residence or ownership changes. First-time homeowners should bring a copy of the warranty deed.

To appeal a value, file with the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. If you remain dissatisfied, the appeal goes to the Board of Equalization and then to Superior Court, or you can choose arbitration. An appeal can address taxability, value or uniformity, and not the size of the tax bill.

  • Owners 65 and older who hold another homestead exemption can also receive an exemption from the state portion of tax on the home and up to 10 acres.
  • A deferral is available to owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less.
  • Real property returns and exemption applications for conservation use must be mailed to the assessors with a postmark no later than April 1.

sections.h2: What should I do about Warner Robins tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Commissioner's Warner Robins office for a payoff, and give the number to your closing attorney or title company. Value is set as of January 1 each year, so the sale contract should say who pays which portion of the year's bill.

If the house was a rental, check the personal property side too. The assessors warn buyers to look for unpaid personal property tax on boats, aircraft and business items, which attorneys tend to overlook.

Owners who inherited a house, fell behind or live out of town can sell as-is to a buyer who pays the county from the proceeds.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Warner Robins?
faqs.a: December 20 of the year the bill is mailed. Houston County normally mails real estate bills before October 20. Mobile homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: What is the Warner Robins city millage rate for 2026?
faqs.a: 10.000 mills, adopted September 22, 2026. The 2025 rate was 8.953 mills, and the rate stayed at 8.953 in 2024. County and school rates are set separately.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Warner Robins property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Houston County Tax Commissioner at 202 Carl Vinson Parkway in Warner Robins or online through the commissioner's site, where a convenience fee applies. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Houston County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, whose real estate line is (478) 218-4750.

faqs.q: Is part of Warner Robins in Peach County?
faqs.a: Yes. The city lies in Houston and Peach counties, and the city's rollback figures treat the two parts separately. If your parcel is in Peach County, ask that county's tax offices where to pay.
